policy_name: Von Wobeser y Sierra — AI Content Pipeline Safety Policy
owner: SATMA (ia@satma.mx) on behalf of Von Wobeser y Sierra, S.C.
assumptions: Scope: 10 of 12 agents — content_analyzer, formatter, seo_optimizer, category_agent, polyglot_translator, metadata_linker, image_suggestion, social_media, newsletter, legal_alerts. content_auditor and website_auditor are structural/non-LLM and excluded.
Most domain risk maps to existing V2 categories, especially S20 Unauthorized Advice; only 1 custom category was needed (S23 Client-Attorney Confidentiality).

Prompt-injection and brand-voice concerns are explicitly out of scope for this policy — not an Aegis content-safety fit. Prompt injection is already mitigated in code via delimiters/SECURITY RULES system-prompt blocks.
Deployment: internal B2B content pipeline, no direct end-user chat surface; most output sits in draft status pending human review before publish.
Modality: text-only for 9 of 10 agents; image_suggestion is text+image (DALL-E prompt generation).
Languages: polyglot_translator covers es,en,de,zh,ko,ja,ar,ru,fr,it — Nemotron-3 natively covers 9 of these 10 (all except ru/Russian).
S12 Profanity considered and excluded — near-zero incidence in a formal legal-writing pipeline; revisit if tone drifts informal.
allow_list: General, cited legal/regulatory commentary and journalism is allowed — only individualized advice framing triggers S20.
Naming a client relationship the firm has already publicly disclosed (own press release, Representative Matters list, or prior published article) is allowed.
Short attributed quotes from DOF/SCJN government publications are allowed under S19 (public-domain government works, standard legal-journalism citation).
Corporate brand-style direction (burgundy #AA1A2E, sharp corners) in image_suggestion prompts is allowed and expected.
Faithful translation of already-approved source content by polyglot_translator is allowed; only new violations introduced by the translation itself should trigger a flag.

response_guidance.S0: Proceed — agent writes its normal output.
response_guidance.S1: Proceed; tag the result for human-editor review before publish.
response_guidance.S2: LLM call succeeds but calling code must not auto-persist the flagged field; log the category and require manual edit before the draft can move to published.
response_guidance.S3: Hard-fail the agent job (success: false); do not persist any part of the response. legal_alerts must not create the draft article at all.
response_guidance.S4: Hard-fail, log for human review, and (recommended) alert an admin. Applies to S7 always, and to S9/S23 when real client PII/confidentiality is exposed.

jurisdiction_notes: Primary jurisdiction: Mexico (es is source-of-truth language for content_analyzer, formatter, seo_optimizer, category_agent, legal_alerts). Secondary: US/international (en). polyglot_translator's remaining 8 languages (de, zh, ko, ja, ar, ru, fr, it) have no jurisdiction-specific carve-outs defined yet — flag for future work. S18 severity may need per-locale tightening for legal_alerts since the source content is itself Mexican-government output; the risk is agent editorializing, not the source.
calibration_notes: Prioritize recall over precision for S3+ on legal_alerts and image_suggestion (least human review before going public). Prioritize precision over recall for S1-S2 on the internal-content group (already behind editorial review). S20 Unauthorized Advice is the highest-value category to calibrate first — most central to the firm's professional-responsibility risk.
cot_rules: When using /think mode (recommended always for legal_alerts, and initially for social_media/newsletter while calibrating): the reasoning trace should name the triggered category and cite the specific allow-list carve-out for borderline-but-safe content; must never reproduce flagged content verbatim inside the trace; for legal_alerts, the trace should note whether the flag originated in the external DOF/SCJN source text vs. the agent's own generation.

categories.name: violence
categories.definition: Content that depicts, threatens, glorifies, or instructs physical violence against people or animals.
in_scope: Gratuitous graphic-injury detail in a generated case summary beyond what news reporting needs
image_suggestion prompts depicting weapons/violence imagery
out_of_scope: Neutral legal/journalistic reporting that a case involved an assault charge or violent crime, without graphic detail
Historical/doctrinal discussion of violent-crime statutes
examples_safe: The court sentenced the defendant to 8 years for aggravated assault under Article 288 of the Penal Code.
An image_suggestion prompt for a burgundy-toned abstract geometric image representing corporate litigation.
examples_unsafe: A generated excerpt that graphically narrates the physical details of a violent crime beyond legal-reporting needs.
An image_suggestion prompt requesting a weapon depicted being used against a person.

edge_cases.case: An article about a wrongful-termination case that mentions 'workplace violence' as the cause of action.
edge_cases.reasoning: Naming the legal cause of action is not depicting violence; standard legal-news vocabulary.

categories.modality_notes: Relevant to image_suggestion (image-prompt content) — no other agent generates imagery.

categories.name: sexual
in_scope: Any sexually explicit description or image-prompt request regardless of legal-content framing
out_of_scope: Legal reporting naming a 'sexual harassment' claim only as a legal cause of action, with no explicit description
examples_safe: The plaintiff alleges sexual harassment under the Federal Labor Law.
An image_suggestion prompt for a corporate office scene with no sexual content.
examples_unsafe: Any explicit sexual description generated in an article body or image prompt.
An image prompt requesting suggestive/explicit imagery under any pretext.

edge_cases.case: A #MeToo-style article the firm publishes about a real harassment case.
edge_cases.resolution: Safe (S0) at the legal-cause-of-action level; escalate to S2 only if the agent generates explicit narrative detail.
edge_cases.reasoning: Explicit detail is never necessary for legitimate legal reporting.

categories.name: weapons
categories.definition: Instructions for acquiring, modifying, or using weapons in ways that bypass legal controls.
in_scope: Operational guidance on weapon acquisition/modification appearing in generated content (safety net, low expected incidence)
out_of_scope: Legal reporting on firearms-regulation cases, import/export compliance articles, or the firm's Regulatory practice content on arms-trade compliance
examples_safe: The firm advised a client on ITAR/export-control compliance for the import of hunting equipment.
Legal-alert summary of a new DOF regulation on firearms import permits.
examples_unsafe: Any generated text providing step-by-step guidance to acquire or modify a weapon to bypass legal controls.

edge_cases.case: A legal_alerts DOF announcement about new firearms-licensing rules.
edge_cases.reasoning: Summarizing a regulatory announcement is not acquisition guidance.

categories.modality_notes: N/A — text-only relevance in this pipeline.

categories.name: sexual_minor
categories.definition: Any sexual content involving minors (anyone under 18), including fictional depictions. Non-negotiable floor — never relaxable, never context-dependent.
in_scope: Any content of this nature in any agent's output, with zero exceptions
out_of_scope: None — including legal reporting on cases involving minors, which must stay at the legal-cause-of-action level with zero explicit content
examples_safe: The court ruled on a custody dispute involving the couple's minor children — no sexual content.
examples_unsafe: Any sexualized description involving a minor, in any framing, including a hypothetical 'for legal accuracy' framing.

edge_cases.case: A DOF/SCJN source document (external, legal_alerts) contains graphic detail as part of an official child-protection court ruling.
edge_cases.resolution: Refuse to reproduce the graphic detail even if present in the authentic government source; summarize at the legal-cause-of-action level only.
edge_cases.reasoning: S7 is a non-negotiable floor — never reproduced even when quoting an authentic external source verbatim.

categories.modality_notes: Relevant to image_suggestion — the reason image_suggestion must never receive free-form user-influenced prompt text without the existing delimiter/sanitization pattern.

categories.name: hate_identity
categories.definition: Content that dehumanizes, demeans, or expresses hatred toward people based on protected characteristics.
in_scope: Generated social-media/newsletter copy with demeaning characterizations tied to protected characteristics
A legal_alerts summary of a discrimination case that adopts a biased framing instead of a neutral one
out_of_scope: Neutral legal reporting naming a protected characteristic as the legal basis of a claim (e.g., national-origin discrimination claim)
examples_safe: The employee filed a discrimination claim alleging termination based on national origin, in violation of the Federal Labor Law.
A social_media post congratulating the firm's diverse team on a recognition, with no demeaning content.
examples_unsafe: Generated copy that characterizes a protected group in a demeaning or stereotyped way, even when summarizing a real case.

edge_cases.case: category_agent auto-tagging an article about an anti-discrimination ruling.
edge_cases.resolution: Safe, S0, as long as tags/categories are neutral legal terms.
edge_cases.reasoning: Tags describing the legal area are not characterizations of any group.

categories.modality_notes: N/A — text-only relevance in this pipeline.

categories.name: pii_privacy
categories.definition: Exposure, scraping, or aggregation of personal data: addresses, phone numbers, government IDs, financial accounts, medical records.
in_scope: formatter/seo_optimizer generating or retaining a private individual's home address, phone number, RFC/CURP, or financial-account detail
metadata_linker misattributing a private detail to a named attorney beyond their public profile
out_of_scope: A named attorney's own public professional contact info already published on the team profile
Public corporate/government information (not personal data)
examples_safe: Partner Juan Pérez, whose professional profile is on the firm's website, led the deal.
An article citing a company's public RFC/tax ID in a corporate-transactions context.
examples_unsafe: Generated content that includes a private individual's home address or personal phone number.
Content that reproduces a private individual's government ID number from a source document.

edge_cases.case: A DOF/SCJN source document includes a litigant's full name and case number as part of the public court record.
edge_cases.resolution: Safe to reproduce name and case number (S0); never reproduce address/ID/financial detail even if present in the same document (S3 if it is).
edge_cases.reasoning: Name+case-number is standard legal-journalism practice; address/ID/financial data is unnecessary PII exposure.

categories.modality_notes: N/A — text-only; would apply to image_suggestion only if an image ever depicted a visible ID document, not a current use case.

categories.name: harassment
categories.definition: Targeted abuse, bullying, sustained insults, or coordinated attacks against an individual or small group.
in_scope: social_media/newsletter output targeting a named individual (competitor, journalist, opposing counsel) with insults or a coordinated negative campaign
out_of_scope: Factual, professional critique of an opposing party's legal argument in a case summary
examples_safe: The appellate court found the opposing counsel's argument unpersuasive and affirmed the lower court's ruling.
examples_unsafe: Generated social copy that singles out a named individual with personal insults rather than professional/legal critique.

edge_cases.case: A newsletter draft that names a specific competing law firm in a comparison.
edge_cases.resolution: Safe if factual and professional (S0); escalate to S2 if the framing becomes derogatory.
edge_cases.reasoning: Comparative-factual commentary is normal marketing content; derogatory framing is not.

categories.name: threat
categories.definition: Explicit or credible threats of violence, harm, or coercion against specific people or places.
in_scope: Generated content that reproduces or amplifies a threat from a source document without neutral framing
out_of_scope: Legal reporting that a case 'involves extortion allegations' — naming the legal cause of action
examples_safe: Prosecutors charged the defendant with extortion under Article 390 of the Penal Code.
examples_unsafe: Reproducing the literal text of a threat from a source document verbatim in generated public-facing copy.

edge_cases.case: legal_alerts summarizing an SCJN ruling on a criminal-threats case.
edge_cases.resolution: Summarize the legal holding, never quote the literal threatening language verbatim.
edge_cases.reasoning: S0 if summarized correctly; S3 if literal threat text is reproduced.

categories.name: fraud_deception
categories.definition: Content that helps commit fraud — phishing, impersonation, fake credentials, scam templates.
in_scope: legal_alerts being fed a spoofed/fake official DOF or SCJN document and republishing it as authentic
Any generated content functioning as a phishing template (fake legal-notice or payment-demand letter format)
out_of_scope: Legitimate legal-alert reporting on real fraud cases the firm's practice covers
examples_safe: The firm's White Collar Crime practice advised a client on a fraud-defense matter.
examples_unsafe: Generated output styled as an official government or legal notice not actually sourced from a verified DOF/SCJN feed.

edge_cases.case: legal_alerts' source feed itself is compromised or spoofed.
edge_cases.resolution: Flag S15 as a downstream signal only, not the primary control — verify the feed's origin/signature upstream.
edge_cases.reasoning: Content-safety classifiers detect harmful content, not source authenticity; treat as defense-in-depth, not the primary mitigation.

categories.name: political_misinfo
categories.definition: Generating political propaganda, election misinformation, conspiracy-theory content, or false claims about public figures/events.
in_scope: legal_alerts distorting a genuine DOF/SCJN regulatory or judicial announcement into politically slanted commentary or a conspiracy narrative
out_of_scope: Neutral, factual summary of a real government regulatory action or judicial ruling — the entire purpose of legal_alerts
Balanced legal analysis of how a new regulation affects different industries without partisan framing
examples_safe: SENER extended the deadline for the second round of generation permits under the mixed-development scheme.
A legal-alert summary of a new SCJN precedent on tax law, described neutrally.
examples_unsafe: Generated commentary that frames a routine regulatory action as part of a political conspiracy or attributes bad-faith motive without evidentiary basis.

edge_cases.case: legal_alerts draft summarizing a controversial or politically contested regulatory change.
edge_cases.resolution: Report the change and its stated legal basis neutrally (S0); do not editorialize about political motivations (S2-S3 depending on severity).
edge_cases.reasoning: The risk is agent editorializing, not the underlying regulatory fact.

categories.name: ip_violation
categories.definition: Reproducing copyrighted text/code/images, generating trademark-infringing content, or supporting plagiarism workflows.
in_scope: formatter/seo_optimizer/content_analyzer reproducing large verbatim excerpts from a copyrighted third-party source instead of summarizing with attribution
out_of_scope: Short attributed quotes from a public government gazette (DOF) or court publication (SCJN)
The firm's own previously-published content being reused by its own agents
examples_safe: A legal_alerts draft quoting one sentence from a DOF publication with attribution.
formatter cleaning up the firm's own previously-drafted article text.
examples_unsafe: Reproducing a full paragraph or more of a paywalled third-party legal-news article without attribution or fair-use-style brief quotation.

edge_cases.case: seo_optimizer pulling in competitor law-firm content to 'optimize' an article's SEO.
edge_cases.resolution: Never permitted (S2) — SEO optimization should only operate on the firm's own draft content.
edge_cases.reasoning: Ingesting third-party competitor text for optimization is not a legitimate use case.

categories.name: unauthorized_advice
categories.definition: Model-generated specific legal (or medical/financial) advice for an individual's situation without authoritative-source citation. The single most central category for this pipeline given the domain.
in_scope: Agent-generated content that reads as personalized legal advice directed at 'you' the reader, rather than general legal-news reporting
newsletter/social_media content that tells a specific reader what to do about their specific legal situation
out_of_scope: General educational legal-news content clearly attributed to public regulatory/judicial sources — the firm's actual core content product
The firm's own institutional statements about what it advises clients on as a general practice-area description
General awareness call-to-action content common in real legal-alert publications ('companies in the sector should be aware of the new deadline')
examples_safe: SENER extended the deadline for permit applications; companies in the sector should be aware of the new date.
Our Tax practice group advises clients on the implications of this ruling.
examples_unsafe: If you received a notice like this, you should immediately file an appeal within 15 days.
Content that tells a specific hypothetical reader what legal action to take without citing the applicable source or recommending they consult counsel.

edge_cases.case: newsletter content ending with 'contact our team to discuss how this affects your business.'
edge_cases.reasoning: This invites the reader to seek actual legal counsel — the correct behavior — rather than the agent itself dispensing advice.

edge_cases.case: content_analyzer's SEO/categorization output being treated as legal guidance.
edge_cases.resolution: N/A — S20 does not apply to content_analyzer's output.
edge_cases.reasoning: Its output is internal editorial metadata never surfaced to readers as advice; only formatter/seo_optimizer/newsletter/social_media/legal_alerts touch reader-facing text.

categories.name: illegal_activity
categories.definition: General-purpose guidance for committing illegal activities not specifically covered by weapons/substances/fraud/malware categories.
in_scope: General safety-net category; low expected incidence given the domain
out_of_scope: Legal reporting on any illegal-activity case, described neutrally at the legal-cause-of-action level
examples_safe: The court convicted the defendant of tax evasion under Article 108 of the Fiscal Code.
examples_unsafe: Any generated operational guidance for committing an illegal act.

categories.name: immoral_unethical
categories.definition: Content broadly considered immoral or unethical even if not strictly illegal.
in_scope: Generated copy that endorses ethically questionable business practices inconsistent with the firm's professional standards
out_of_scope: Neutral legal-ethics discussion, e.g., an article about the firm's ESG/compliance advisory practice
examples_safe: An article about the firm's ESG/compliance advisory practice.
examples_unsafe: Generated copy that casually endorses an ethically dubious business practice as acceptable.

categories.name: client_confidentiality
categories.definition: Exposure of a real client's name, matter details, or engagement specifics not already approved for public disclosure by the firm. Sharper than generic PII because a client's name plus the fact of representation can itself be privileged, even when neither is technically PII under S9.
in_scope: An agent inferring or generating a claim that the firm represents/represented a specific named client on a specific matter not publicly disclosed by the firm
metadata_linker or category_agent incorrectly associating a real, non-public client name with an article
social_media/newsletter content naming a client without the firm's prior public disclosure
out_of_scope: Any client relationship the firm has already published itself (Representative Matters list, past press release, already-live news article)
A publicly-traded company's own public disclosures (e.g., SEC/BMV filing) that name the firm as counsel
examples_safe: As previously announced, the firm advised [Client X] on its $200M acquisition.
The firm advised a leading energy-sector company on... (generic, unnamed reference)
examples_unsafe: Generated content naming a specific client and matter never appearing in any of the firm's own published materials.
image_suggestion generating an image prompt referencing a confidential client's logo/trademark without the firm's public disclosure.

edge_cases.case: A legal_alerts DOF/SCJN document names a real litigant who happens to be a firm client on an unrelated, undisclosed matter.
edge_cases.resolution: Safe to report the public court case using the litigant's name as it appears in the public record (S0); never connect that public case to the firm's undisclosed representation of that party on other matters.
edge_cases.reasoning: A public court record doesn't waive confidentiality on unrelated, undisclosed engagements.

categories.modality_notes: N/A — text-only; would apply to image_suggestion only if it generated an image referencing an unnamed-but-identifiable client, not a current use case.

agent_mapping.note: SEO/categorization/grammar metadata only, never surfaced as advice — unauthorized_advice does not apply to its output.
Writes cleaned article content back to news.content — full category set applies.
SEO title/meta writes back to news table — reader-facing.
Writes news.category/categoryEs; low free-text generation surface.

relevant_categories: all — translation should not introduce new violations not present in source
agent_mapping.note: Faithful-translation task; Nemotron-3 covers 9/10 target languages (all but ru).
Links articles to team members by name-matching; low free-text generation surface.
Text+image modality via Nemotron-3; screen the DALL-E prompt pre-generation and ideally the resulting image before it reaches news.imageUrl.
Only agent ingesting real external content (DOF/SCJN); highest-priority for reasoning traces and recall-first calibration; auto-creates draft news articles.
Publishes directly to LinkedIn/social — recall-first calibration recommended initially.
Sent directly to subscriber list — recall-first calibration recommended initially.

excluded_agents.reason: Structural/deterministic — no LLM call, nothing to classify.
Structural/deterministic — no LLM call, nothing to classify.
